spec: CONTROL.md §6 `fork`, A copy is the session as it was
note: Whether a session's copy is out of date, so the next message for the session gets a fresh copy rather than this one. `last_ran` is when a message last ran in the copy, as the copy's record says (its `used`, else its `at`; empty: a record that never said). `session_written_s` is when the session's own transcript was last written, in seconds relative to `last_ran` (negative: before it). A write while the copy's run was going on is one the copy never saw. `expect`: `stale` (forget it, copy the session again) or `current` (keep sending the session's messages to it).

cases.name: the session was written to a day after its copy last ran
not written to since the copy last ran
written while the copy's run was still going, a second after it began
written in the same instant the copy's run began
a record that never said when (0.10.0 and earlier wrote the id alone)
